text.content: As Contigo GmbH expands its agent capabilities, the development team runs into a recurring confusion. Developers are storing policy documents in the conversation memory. Others are using the knowledge base to track user preferences. One team is mixing live API calls with document retrieval in ways that make the system unpredictable and difficult to debug.

rich_text.plain_text: As Contigo GmbH expands its agent capabilities, the development team runs into a recurring confusion. Developers are storing policy documents in the conversation memory. Others are using the knowledge base to track user preferences. One team is mixing live API calls with document retrieval in ways that make the system unpredictable and difficult to debug.

text.content: The root cause is the same in every case: the three core components of a business agent (memory, knowledge base, and tool state) are being treated as interchangeable but they are not.  Each serves a unique purpose that ensures that agents are reliable, maintained, and easier to trust.

text.content: A knowledge base is a collection of documents or records the agent can search when it needs factual information. Rather than relying on the language model's general training, the agent retrieves content from verified sources to ground its responses. You will build this in Sprint 2.

text.content: Keeping these three components separate is a prerequisite for building agents that are safe, auditable, and maintainable. An agent that conflates memory with retrieval will struggle to find the right information. An agent that conflates retrieval with tool use may act on documents instead of querying live systems, or vice versa.

Takeaway:

text.content: Memory, knowledge base, and tool state are three distinct components with three distinct jobs. Memory tracks the conversation. The knowledge base grounds the response in verified facts. Tools take action in the real world. A reliable business agent keeps these separate. This sprint covers memory. The other two components will be built in the sprints that follow.
